Most coasts see two high tides a day because the moon pulls on the water on its near side and, in effect, on the far side of the Earth as well. This paragraph is long enough for Readability to keep it as the main content of the page.

A second paragraph explains the spring tide, which happens when the sun and moon line up, and links to the data with more words so the article clearly outweighs the navigation.

A third paragraph closes the post with a few more sentences, so that the text density of the article stays well above that of the rest of the page.
